item.title: Japan Launches Its First Commercial Floating Offshore Wind Farm at Goto
item.description: Toda Construction announced that its consortium has commenced commercial operations at the Goto Offshore Wind Farm in Nagasaki Prefecture, marking Japan’s first-ever commercial floating offshore wind project. Officially certified under Japan’s Marine Renewable Energy Sea-Area Utilisation Act, the 16.8 megawatt (MW) facility makes Japan one of the nations advancing floating wind from pilot to full-scale deployment. item.title: Vayona Energy Appoints Pritesh Vinay CEO After Siemens Gamesa Onshore Wind Deal
item.description: Wind turbine original equipment manufacturer (OEM) Vayona Energy, which operates across India and South Asia, has appointed Pritesh Vinay as its new Chief Executive Officer (CEO), effective January 5, 2026. The appointment marks a key milestone in Vayona Energy’s evolution as an independent platform following its acquisition of Siemens Gamesa’s onshore wind business in India and Sri Lanka, the company said in a press release. item.title: IEX Q3 FY’26: From Cheap Power to Tightening Prices as Buyers Shift from DAM to TAM
item.description: The Indian Energy Exchange (IEX), the country’s premier marketplace for electricity, delivered strong double-digit volume growth in Q3 FY’26 even as market conditions shifted sharply by December. The quarter marked a transition from a surplus-driven, low-price environment to a tightening landscape with rising prices and evolving trading strategies. item.title: Gujarat: SECI Issues EPC Tender for Five 160 MVA Transformers, Backing 700 MW Solar Project
item.description: The Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) has issued an EPC tender for the commissioning of five units of 160 MVA, 220/33–33 kV power transformers at RadhaNesda in Gujarat. The power supplied from the transformers under this tender will be utilised for a 700 MW (AC) ground-mounted solar power plant to be established at Radhanesda, Gujarat. item.title: LONGI Ditches Silver for Base Metals as Solar Industry Faces Price Crunch
item.description: LONGI Green Energy Technology announced on Monday that it will begin replacing silver with base metals in its solar cell production. This is in line with the industry’s response to the metal's unprecedented price surge. The Chinese manufacturer plans to commence mass production using the new material composition in the second quarter, a move expected to substantially reduce the manufacturing cost of solar modules. item.title: Nordex Secures 508 MW Canadian Wind Order with N175 Turbine Market Entry
item.description: The Germany based Nordex Group has revealed it secured repeat orders in Canada for the supply and installation of a total of 73 wind turbines. item.title: Green Stocks Jan 06- Emmvee Shines As A Value Play
item.description: Stocks continued to struggle in weak conditions, with recently listed solar manufacturer Emmvee Photovoltaic taking off today on strong broker recommendations as a value play. Calling it 'compelling', the brokerage saw a 70% upside, of which about 10% was recovered today. item.title: Solar, Wind Push Germany’s Renewables Power Mix to 58.8% in 2025
item.description: Germany recorded 437.6 terawatt hours (TWh) of actual power generation in 2025, almost unchanged from 437.7 TWh in 2024. Of the total generation mix, renewables accounted for 257.5 TWh, or 58.8%, compared with 58.5% in 2024. Germany’s power generation declined marginally from 437.7 TWh in 2024 to 437.6 TWh in 2025, marking a 0.02% year-on-year (YoY) decrease. item.title: Even As Monsoon Dampens Demand & Solar CUF Falls to 16.5%, SBI Caps Predicts better CY 26 For Solar
item.description: As India closed 2025, energy sector demand rose, led by an above-average monsoon, which curtailed cooling demand in the North and broadly dampened industrial and agricultural needs.
